blocks.text: The Math Behind MWF (13.0 Visits/Mo) vs. Tuesday/Thursday (8.66 Visits/Mo)

When US office managers request bids for part-week commercial cleaning, they frequently ask contractors for both a 3x-weekly Monday/Wednesday/Friday (MWF) quote and a 2x-weekly Tuesday/Thursday (Tue/Thu) quote. At first glance, dropping from three visits per week to two visits per week looks like an automatic 33.3% cost reduction. In reality, commercial janitorial pricing never drops by the full 33.3% because spacing visits 48 to 96 hours apart increases the soil load, trash volume, and restroom descaling time required during each individual visit.

Using the industry-standard 4.33 weeks per month (52 weeks ÷ 12 months), a 2x-weekly Tuesday/Thursday schedule equals exactly 8.66 visits per month and serves as the 1.00x baseline frequency multiplier in commercial estimating software. A 3x-weekly Monday/Wednesday/Friday schedule equals 13.0 visits per month and earns a 0.95x per-visit frequency multiplier because shorter 48-hour intervals between cleanings allow technicians to move faster through vacuuming, dusting, and restroom wipe-downs. Understanding how that 5% per-visit efficiency discount interacts with 4.34 extra monthly visits is essential for accurate facility budgeting.

blocks.title: Why Net Monthly Savings Average 29.8%, Not 33.3%
blocks.text: Take a 10,000 sq ft carpeted office (1.00x flooring multiplier) with a $0.10/sq ft baseline 2x-weekly rate. On a Tue/Thu schedule (8.66 visits × 1.00x multiplier), the visit price is $1,000 and the monthly invoice is $8,660. On an MWF schedule (13.0 visits × 0.95x multiplier), the visit price drops to $950, bringing the monthly invoice to $12,350. Moving from MWF to Tue/Thu saves $3,690/month—an exact 29.88% reduction.

blocks.text: In addition to base square-foot labor, remember to account for per-visit add-on frequencies. If your contract itemizes restroom sanitation ($15 to $30 per visit), breakroom and kitchenette detailing ($12 to $25 per visit), and interior partition glass ($15 to $35 per visit) as per-visit line items, dropping from 13.0 visits to 8.66 visits automatically trims those three add-on lines by 4.34 occurrences per month. Conversely, monthly amortized programs—such as quarterly deep floor care at $0.03 to $0.06 per sq ft per month—remain unchanged regardless of whether nightly crews arrive two or three times a week.
The Weekend Bridge Problem: Friday Night vs. Thursday Night Cleanings

The most critical operational difference between an MWF and a Tuesday/Thursday visit split is what happens between Thursday at 5:00 PM and Monday at 8:00 AM. Under a Monday/Wednesday/Friday evening schedule, the Friday night crew purges all breakroom refrigerators, removes food wrappers from central trash hubs, sanitizes restrooms, and leaves the facility pristine for Monday morning arrival.

Under a standard Tuesday/Thursday evening schedule, the last clean of the week happens Thursday night. Any coffee grounds, catered Friday lunch boxes, restroom paper waste, or mud tracked into the lobby during Friday's workday sits untouched in the building for 96 straight hours—from Thursday night until Tuesday evening after work! Furthermore, employees arriving Monday morning walk into Friday's uncleaned office and must wait another full workday and a half before the Tuesday night crew arrives.

blocks.title: Why Many 'Tuesday/Thursday' Contracts Shift to Tuesday/Friday
blocks.text: If your office has more than 15% occupancy on Fridays, a literal Tuesday/Thursday night schedule creates fruit-fly and odor issues over the 72-hour weekend and leaves Monday morning dirty. Ask your vendor to shift your 2x-weekly 8.66-visit schedule to Tuesday Night + Friday Night (at the exact same 1.00x pricing multiplier) so the office is always reset before the weekend lockup.
Crew Productivity and Backpack Vacuum Ergonomics on Split Schedules

Because part-week schedules allow 48 to 72 hours of foot-traffic grit, carpet fiber shedding, and paper dust to accumulate between visits, vacuuming consumes up to 40% of total on-site labor hours during an MWF or Tue/Thu shift. Relying on household upright vacuums cuts production rates from the ISSA commercial benchmark of 3,500 sq ft/hour down to 1,800 sq ft/hour, forcing contractors to bill more hours at $35 to $65/hour.

blocks.text: Security Lockup, Alarm Windows, and HVAC Override Costs

In commercial properties where after-hours janitorial visits trigger building security check-ins, alarm arm/disarm fees, or minimum 2-hour HVAC/lighting zone extensions, cutting 4.34 visits per month (from 13.0 on MWF down to 8.66 on Tue/Thu) creates secondary facility savings beyond the janitorial invoice.

items.name: Step 1: Verify Route Consolidation Discounts on Tue/Thu Nights
items.text: Because Monday, Wednesday, and Friday nights are peak demand nights for commercial janitorial companies, some regional contractors offer an extra 3% to 5% hourly rate concession ($35–$48/hr vs. $42–$55/hr) if you accept a Tuesday/Thursday or Tuesday/Saturday route slot that utilizes their midweek crew capacity.

items.name: Step 2: Align Building Alarm & Keycard Windows to Exact Visit Nights
items.text: Program your access control panel so the vendor's PIN and keycards only disarm the suite on your exact contract nights (e.g., Tue/Thu 6:30 PM – 9:30 PM), automatically rejecting off-night entry attempts.

items.name: Step 3: Audit Per-Visit vs. Flat-Monthly Contract Wording
items.text: Confirm your contract states a fixed monthly price based on 13.0 visits (MWF) or 8.66 visits (Tue/Thu) across 4.33 weeks, and specifies a pro-rata credit (Monthly Fee ÷ 13.0 or 8.66) whenever a scheduled visit falls on an observed building holiday and is not rescheduled.

faqs.q: Why does a 2x-weekly Tuesday/Thursday cleaning cost more per visit than a 3x-weekly MWF cleaning?
faqs.a: Commercial estimators apply a 1.00x frequency multiplier to 2x-weekly service (8.66 visits/month) and a 0.95x multiplier to 3x-weekly service (13.0 visits/month). When 48 to 96 hours pass between cleanings on a 2x-weekly schedule, trash cans are fuller, restroom fixtures have heavier mineral and soap buildup, and carpets hold more tracked-in grit, requiring roughly 5% more labor minutes per visit than a 3x-weekly schedule.

faqs.q: How do contractors arrive at 13.0 visits for MWF and 8.66 visits for Tuesday/Thursday?
faqs.a: There are 52 weeks in a year, not 48 (4 weeks × 12 months = 48 weeks, which misses 4 full weeks of service per year). Dividing 52 weeks by 12 months yields 4.333 weeks per month. Multiplying 3 visits/week × 4.333 equals 13.0 visits/month for MWF; multiplying 2 visits/week × 4.333 equals 8.66 visits/month for Tuesday/Thursday.

faqs.q: Can we switch our 2x-weekly schedule from Tuesday/Thursday to Wednesday/Friday without a rate increase?
faqs.a: In 95% of US commercial janitorial contracts, yes. The 2x-weekly 1.00x frequency multiplier and 8.66 monthly visit count apply to any two fixed weekday evenings per week—whether Tuesday/Thursday, Tuesday/Friday, or Wednesday/Friday. Many hybrid offices prefer Tuesday/Friday or Wednesday/Friday so weekend trash never sits in the breakroom from Thursday night until Tuesday.

faqs.q: How do paper and soap consumable charges change between MWF and Tuesday/Thursday schedules?
faqs.a: While the benchmark consumables formula lists $0.012 to $0.025 per sq ft per visit, actual toilet tissue, hard-roll paper towel, and foam soap consumption is driven by weekly employee headcount, not whether the janitor restocks the dispensers two times or three times per week. If you downgrade from MWF to Tue/Thu without reducing employee attendance, ensure the crew leaves extra stocked rolls inside the dispenser cabinets so stalls do not run dry on Mondays or Fridays.

faqs.q: What happens when a federal holiday lands on a Monday under an MWF contract?
faqs.a: Because most US federal holidays (Memorial Day, Labor Day, MLK Day, Presidents' Day, Indigenous Peoples' Day) fall on Mondays, an MWF schedule loses 6 to 8 Monday service nights per year compared to only 1 Thursday holiday (Thanksgiving) on a Tue/Thu schedule. Ensure your MWF contract requires the vendor either to shift holiday Monday visits to Tuesday night or issue a 1/13th monthly invoice credit for skipped holiday visits.
